# massdriver_stash_entry (Resource)

Alpha: this resource can change or be removed at any time.

An entry in the Massdriver stash of a project, environment, component, instance, or deployment. A write replaces the whole entry. Creating this resource overwrites an entry that already has the key. Changing the scope or the key replaces the entry. Changing an immutable entry deletes it and writes it again. Do not use `create_before_destroy` with this resource: the old and new entries have the same key, so deleting the old entry deletes the new one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A value with a label shows as a row on the instance's Metadata tab.
resource "massdriver_stash_entry" "db_hostname" {
  instance = "ecomm-prod-db"
  key      = "db/hostname"
  value    = aws_db_instance.main.address
  label    = "Database host"
}

# Runbook and product links show as buttons in the environment header.
resource "massdriver_stash_entry" "links" {
  environment = "ecomm-prod"
  key         = "md/v1/links"
  format      = "JSON"
  value = jsonencode({
    links = [
      { label = "Runbook", url = "https://wiki.example.com/ecomm" },
      { label = "Shop", url = "https://shop.example.com" },
    ]
  })
}

# A bundle records what runs on its instance. Inside a bundle deployment, the
# provider signs in with the deployment's token.
resource "massdriver_stash_entry" "release" {
  instance = "ecomm-prod-api"
  key      = "md/v1/release"
  format   = "JSON"
  value = jsonencode({
    version = var.app_version
    image   = "${var.image_repository}:${var.image_tag}"
  })
}

# A secret that a later deployment reads. Massdriver encrypts it, and
# Terraform hides it in plan output.
resource "massdriver_stash_entry" "kubeconfig" {
  environment     = "ecomm-prod"
  key             = "kubeconfig"
  sensitive_value = module.cluster.kubeconfig
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) The entry's key. Letters, digits, and the characters `_`, `.`, `/`, and `-`, up to 255 characters. Keys that start with `md/` are well-known keys. The server checks their values against a schema.

### Optional

- `component` (String) Identifier of the component whose stash holds the entry, such as `ecomm-db`. Set exactly one of `project`, `environment`, `component`, `instance`, or `deployment`.
- `deployment` (String) UUID of the deployment whose stash holds the entry. Inside a bundle deployment, this is the `MASSDRIVER_DEPLOYMENT_ID` environment variable. Set exactly one of `project`, `environment`, `component`, `instance`, or `deployment`.
- `environment` (String) Identifier of the environment whose stash holds the entry, such as `ecomm-prod`. Set exactly one of `project`, `environment`, `component`, `instance`, or `deployment`.
- `format` (String) How the value is read: `TEXT` or `JSON`. A `JSON` value must be a JSON object. Defaults to `TEXT`.
- `immutable` (Boolean) When `true`, the server refuses a second write to the key. A change to any argument of an immutable entry deletes the entry and writes it again. Defaults to `false`.
- `instance` (String) Identifier of the instance whose stash holds the entry, such as `ecomm-prod-db`. Set exactly one of `project`, `environment`, `component`, `instance`, or `deployment`.
- `label` (String) A name for the entry, up to 255 characters. An entry with a label shows as a row on the Metadata panels. A label is not encrypted, so do not put secrets in it.
- `project` (String) Identifier of the project whose stash holds the entry, such as `ecomm`. Set exactly one of `project`, `environment`, `component`, `instance`, or `deployment`.
- `sensitive_value` (String, Sensitive) The entry's value, stored as a sensitive entry. Massdriver encrypts it. Only a caller with `stash:export`, or a deployment token, can read it. Terraform hides it in plan output. Set exactly one of `value` or `sensitive_value`. A key that starts with `md/` cannot be sensitive.
- `ttl` (Number) Seconds until the entry expires, up to 315360000 (10 years). `0` keeps the entry until it is deleted. Each write starts the time again. After the entry expires, the next plan shows it as missing and the next apply writes it again. Do not use Terraform to manage a value that must expire and stay gone.
- `value` (String) The entry's value. Use `jsonencode` for a `JSON` entry. Set exactly one of `value` or `sensitive_value`. A `value` shows in plan output.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `sensitive` (Boolean) Whether the entry is sensitive. It is `true` when `sensitive_value` is set.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is <kind>:<scope-id>/<key>, where kind is project,
# environment, component, instance, or deployment. The API does not return
# `ttl`, or a sensitive value that the caller cannot read, so when the
# configuration sets them, the next apply writes the entry again. For an
# immutable entry, that write deletes the entry first.
terraform import massdriver_stash_entry.links environment:ecomm-prod/md/v1/links
```
